_: The ground's look (land3d.gd, terrain.gd read it through data.gd; docs/TUNING.md). The painted look (art-direction/concept-town-repaint.png; Foundation and Tiny Glade's soft painted ground): layers: Terrain3D's ground layers, each a painting of the look audit's painted ground (assets/ground/painted_v2, docs/art/ground/sheet.jpg; packed by tools/pack_painted_ground.gd into assets/ground/terrain3d), its scale (texture repeats per game unit: the paintings are about 4 m a tile, 2 a unit) and, if ever needed, a tint (multiplies it; the paint is final, none now); a wider beach, no surf at the shore. beach.top: how far above the waterline the shore's ground runs, ramping in to the water (game units; 0.07: a soft blend, WC3's shores through dirt; at 0.015 in rock it drew a hard yellow stroke round every coast, g30), beach.layer the ground it is. beach.snow: [below, from] heights (game units) between which winter's snow comes in over the shore: none on the tide-washed beach below the first, whole from the second (g10 crossing: the beach white as snow). roads: a grass verge either side of each track (verge: its width as a share of the road's; vergeTint: its colour and strength, near the grass's own so it blends, not a yellow band); tint: every road's, street's and track's earth, a multiply on the painted road (assets/ground/painted_v2/dirt_road.png; 1: as painted); kingsShade: the King's road that much darker; edge: how a track frays into the grass (feather: the soft edge's width as a share of the road's; wander: how far its verges wander in and out; crown: how solid the grassy strip down the middle stays, 1 none; ruts: how dark the two wheel ruts; ends: how far each stretch's ends fray out, as a share of a tile, so the stretches of a street overlap softly instead of ending square, batch 6 (c)). wear (wear.gd): paths worn where people walk (only where they moved at least walkMin units since the last stamp: standing people wear no pads); on, how much a step wears (0..1), how much grows back each upload, how often people are stamped and the wear uploaded (seconds), the bare earth's colour. macro: Terrain3D's broad colour patches over every layer (research #3, the big low-frequency hue tint): two colours (a lush green, a sun-dried yellow), scale the patches' noise (lower is broader; Terrain3D noise1_scale), slope how much slopes take it; set whether the ground is painted or not. painting: which of the painted set's textures the layer draws (the look audit's painted ground, assets/ground/painted_v2; packed by tools/pack_painted_ground.gd into assets/ground/terrain3d); every layer takes one (tools/ground_check.gd fails a layer that doesn't); lift: how far the painting is washed toward white (the pack has no snow: the snow is its palest stone, lifted). winter.snow: the colour winter's snow lies in, over the land, the roofs (snow.gdshader) and the leaves (snow_leaf.gdshader) alike (g24 raid: roofs at 0.9 and the land at 0.74 blew out near white; g25: 0.66-0.79 read as grey mud, now 0.74-0.86, a soft blue-white between); winter.paint: how much of the painted ground (roads, squares, fields, worn paths: terrain.gd paint) the snow hides at full cover, so tracks show as trodden lines, never orange through it (g25 raid) (land3d.gd snow_col; was 0.84, 0.86, 0.91: the light pass found the square's blown whites were mostly snow, so about 0.88 of it, its blue cast kept). mesh: Terrain3D's rings of land round the lens (size: vertices across the finest ring, each further ring twice as coarse; lods: how many rings). Its default 48 drew the mid zoom's ground from points 2 units apart, sinking a lake's low shore under the water's surface (the grey smear, fields seen lying on the lake); 128 keeps half-unit detail out to about 30 units. rivers (rivers.gd): never a square end. mouthUnder: how far under the sea's or a lake's surface a river's mouth sinks (game units); mouthEase: over how many of its last points (half a unit apart) it eases down; taper: over how many points a spring's head or a river running into another narrows; thin: how narrow, as a share of its width; water: how near the river mask (rivers-mask.png, 1 the channel's core, fading over 3 units past the bank) must read for the ground to count as river water, never stood on (terrain.gd in_river; the drawn water reaches mask 0.9 at its bank); lengthDivs: cross-sections of the water's mesh per Waterways step (a step is about the river's width: at 1 its straight sides cut the bends and lay flat sheets over the banks); shallow, deep: the water's colour (the old peaty 0.2/0.26/0.2 read near black from the mid zoom).
_layers: Each layer's painting (painted_v2), its scale (repeats a game unit: lower is larger; the grass 1.0 so the drawn-back view reads no speckle) and calm, applied when tools/pack_painted_ground.gd packs it: contrast (how much of each texel's difference from the painting's mean stays), sat (saturation kept), mult (a colour multiply): WC3's low-contrast tiles (docs/research/terrain-wc3-method.md; g30 landuse, Mac: oversaturated yellow-green speckle). macro a/b: the large soft wash over it, dark and lush green, never yellow.

terrain._: g37 (vs 02-realm: green hills, rock on crests, snow on peaks): Hills grass with stony ground and a little rock (was rock 0.6 over grass 0.5, every hill tile grey rock); Mountains rock over grass 0.6/0.3 (was 1/0.1); Glacier and Tundra no flat snow (was snow 1 and 0.3: tile-shaped white sheets at any height); snow lies only by height (peaks.snow). The ground by Freeciv's terrain (terrain.gd tile_mix; land3d.gd lays the strongest layer over the grass, blended across tile edges): each terrain's weights of the ground layers in land3d.gd's order: grass, dirt (the painted earth), sand, snow, rock, forest, mud, field, dry grass, stony. A river tile (Grassland|river) takes its terrain's. Water tiles are grass here: the beach and the sea floor come from the land's height. patches: a list of patches through the grass, each its own noise: worn earth (Mac, pass 2159: one flat lawn outside the towns; 01-town and 03-army show bare earth and varied ground), drier grass in large soft drifts and darker woodland floor (g33 landuse: one flat green; WC3's large soft variation): layer (its index), most (its weight at a patch's heart, times the tile's grass), from (the noise level where a patch starts: higher, fewer), soft (how far it frays), scale (noise per game unit: higher, smaller patches).
terrain._patches: g38 battle and muster lawns read one flat green: the overlay blend is patch/(grass+patch), so most 0.75 topped out near 0.4 and the height blend mostly kept the grass. Now a lawn is four grounds as WC3 blends them: worn dirt (1), a broad dry-grass wash (8) and a near-scale dry tuft (8 again, scale 0.6), dark floor (5) and rough stony patches (9).

tiers._: terrain.gd _terrace: the hills stepped into shelves with steep faces between (WC3's cliff levels), above from (game units): each step of height a shelf, its last ramp share rising to the next; fading in over over; never by a river. g35: a step every 0.9 drew the hills as nine thin contour stripes; every 2.0 from 2.0 up to 7.0, three bold shelves (WC3's two or three cliff levels). g36: off. Stepping the eroded heightmap drew a cliff contour round every hill at every level, rice terraces across the east; WC3's cliffs are placed by hand, not cut by height, so the hills are AoE2's smooth sun-shaded slopes with rock only where steep (docs/research/terrain-wc3-method.md point 4).

blend._: land3d.gd: Terrain3D's blend_sharpness, how hard one ground gives way to the next (it blends by each layer's painted height; 0.87 snapped the bright snow over with a hard rim, g36). 0.5: soft painted transitions (WC3).

paint._: terrain.gd paint: every painted ground (roads, fields, squares, worn paths) fades where the ground under it turns steep (Godot Decal.normal_fade: 0 never; 0.5 gone on a face steeper than about 60 degrees), so a decal by a bank never streaks down the slope (g38 siege).

auto._: land3d.gd _control_from_land: the auto shader (rock on cliffs, by slope) only where the ground is this steep or bare grass; cliff, the normal's height under which it is a cliff (lower, fewer cliffs).
auto._slope: g38 realm: no rock on any crest, the hills mottled olive: cliff 0.88 (was 0.82, about 35 degrees; now about 28), between g37's gully stripes (0.94) and none; layers.rock.calm contrast 1.0, sat 0.7 (were 0.75, 0.62): the slabs' light and shadow kept, so a crest reads as stone, not grey paint. slope: Terrain3D auto_slope, how soon a slope turns rock (higher: gentler slopes rock; was 1.6, the hills read as grass mounds); high: auto_height_reduction, rock creeping over high ground (0, was 4: g34's realm view had every upland rock from height alone, one cold grey-blue skin with no peak standing out; rock now only where it is steep: crests, tier faces, cliffs; slope 2.0, was 2.6). g37: still grey stripes down every eroded gully: cliff 0.82 (was 0.94, rock from about 20 degrees), slope 1.4 (was 2.0). layers.rock.calm warmed (mult 0.98, 0.94, 0.86, was 0.92, 0.94, 0.98; sat 0.62, was 0.5): 02-realm's mountains are warm brown-grey, not blue.

seasons._: terrain.gd SEASONS: each season's multiply on the leaves, the pines, the grass and the ground ([r, g, b]) and its snow (0-1: the leaves' (weather.json leaves.cover), roofs' (weather.json roof.snow) and low plants' snow read it). Mac 2026-11-14, 'the winter is too harsh, everything is white like crazy, just make it milder': winter's snow 0.25 (was 0.5), its grass dead straw (0.76, 0.76, 0.66; was a grey 0.85, 0.85, 0.82) and its ground a muddy grey-brown (0.82, 0.8, 0.74; was a blue-grey 0.8, 0.82, 0.86), pines darker (Mac: 'think game of thrones', Winterfell's grey and muddy winter), Manor Lords' and Anno 1800's light winters.

winter._: land3d.gd's ground snow (Mac 2026-11-14: too harsh, make it milder; Manor Lords', Anno 1800's light winters). cover: how deep it lies (0-1; was a full 1, every lawn white): at 0.55 it fills the ground's hollows and leaves the rises showing. patch: how much it lies in broad patches (0 even, 1 only in them), patch_scale their size (higher, smaller); high [from, whole]: heights where it lies whole whatever the patches (the hills and peaks keep their snow). trod: how much thinner it lies on the town's trodden earth and fields (0.95: roads and squares dark, was 0.6). paint: how much of a road's or square's paint the snow hides (0.35, was 0.75: roads stay trodden dark).

hosts._: wear.gd _facts: a host in the field wears a camp where it stands (radius camp + camp_per_men x sqrt(men), at most camp_max, game units; step a reading) and a track along the land route it moved by (track: its half-width as a share of the camp's; only moves under track_most units).

gates._: wear.gd _facts: the trodden ground at every town gate: out (game units the worn path runs out), half (its half-width at the gate), spread (how much wider it fans by its end), worn (how much).

roads._: wear.gd _facts: Freeciv's roads wear their verges (width: half-width, game units; worn: how much; floor: the share of it that never grows back; per_reading: links laid each reading).

dual._: land3d.gd: the grass's second, larger scale blended in between near and far (game units from the lens), reduction its size against the first.

peaks._: land3d.gd _control_from_land, terrain.gd _layers_at: snow on the mountains, from snow[0] game units, whole at snow[1] (7.4 to 9.6: only the peaks, soft-edged over 2.2 units; g34: the snow lay as flat white paper patches; 6.2 to 7.8 in 922ecaa2 spread them further). ragged: the snow's edge jittered this much in height by noise of scale (a game unit), so it lies in drifts, not as a shelf's flat sheet with a hard rim (g35). tiers.to: above it the hills stop stepping, so peaks rise whole.

physics._: ground.gd, the one answer to where a body may stand, asked of Jolt (the project's physics engine) through PhysicsServer3D: every obstacle a static prism on a named layer (layers: name -> layer number 1-32; a claim's kind on its own layer where named here, 'host <id>' on host, any other kind on claim), every ask one engine query. tall: half a prism's height (world units: the asks are at height 0). chunk: world units of a source's (the woods') body, its trunks read again there when they change. bin: world units of a town's or a place's body (a piece set down or taken away refills only its bin). land_cell: world units of a cell of the land's dry/walk mask (a block read off the terrain the first time an ask touches it; a cell is dry only where its four corners are); land_block: world units of land read at once (terrain.gd dry_rect).

nav._: The realm's one navigation (nav_world.gd: Godot's NavigationServer3D, Recast navmeshes baked from the land on worker threads and kept). chunk: world units a side of each baked piece (one region per layer); bodies: one navigation map per body size (Godot's way for agents of different widths), radius world units kept off everything standing, cell the map's cell size (walk 0.05: a footpath 0.15 is three cells, a street 0.34 seven, the narrowest gap a walker passes about 0.17; 0.025 baked 4x the cells and polygons for nothing a walker meets): walk (people), wide (a horse, a cart, the roads' planning), host (a host's column on the march), engine (a siege tower or ram rolling to the wall: its half-width kept off every regiment's block); water: the ships' map (sea and lakes deeper than draft below the sea's surface; radius a hull's half beam kept off the shore, a whole number of its cells: Recast rounds it up and warns). open_cost: what open land costs against a street, a road or a town's footpath (the ways layer, cost 1): people keep to the streets, carts and hosts to the roads; river_cost: what fording a river's water costs where no road fords it (wide and host only: a walker never wades); slope: degrees a body climbs; climb: world units of a step up; height: world units a body stands; settle: seconds a chunk's inputs must hold still since their LAST change before it is baked afresh, once (a debounce: a town rising step by step, a road painting stretch by stretch); claims_settle: the same when only held ground changed (a standing block carved or let go; a moving block is never baked round); settle_most: seconds from a chunk's first change it is baked even while its inputs never stop changing; land_every: seconds between layings of bakes on their maps (all landed bakes in one frame: each laying makes the server rebuild the map's edge connections on its next physics step); at_once: bakes on worker threads at a time; watch: chunks looked over a frame for change; confirm_frames: frames a map iteration must stand alone after every chunk's region was built before the map is called ready (nav_world.gd _confirm). hold_still: game seconds (the game's own speed: 4x counts four a second) a claim (a regiment's block, an engine) must hold the same ground before it is carved out of the maps (moving, it is only an avoidance obstacle: army_melee.gd), hold_still_engine the same for an engine's ground (a camp's tower, a parked ram: carved as soon as it stands). hold_slop: how far (world units, any corner) a standing block may sway and still stand (carved where it began). hold_scan seconds between looks. engine_room: how much further a host's map keeps off a siege engine's ground (a regiment's block is wider than its middle: it passes a standing catapult clear). join_reach: how far past the map's own end a route goes on straight to its mark where that ground may be stood on (a man joining his own regiment's block, carved out of the map; mover.gd). avoid: each body kind's radius in a crowd's avoidance (Godot's RVO, mover.gd join): man, horse, cart, engine. straight: a route shorter than this (world units) on clear ground (mover.gd _clear_leg: nothing stands on it, off every engine) goes straight, the map unasked: each ask costs ~2 ms however short, and a field battle's men asked one a cell step (Mac 2026-11-17 "fix the FPS"). closest_rings: how many rings of chunks round a point the nearest-point ask (nav_world.gd _nearest: each chunk's regions, not the whole map, 8 ms a call) looks through before it asks the whole map (open sea, a mark far off every map). ask_s: seconds a route the map cannot give whole (its far end on chunks not landed) is asked before the body walks the landed part toward its mark and asks again from there (mover.gd).

bulk._lighter: bulk.gd lighter: a small plant drawn from its own coarser level (its bake's meshoptimizer levels), by a word of its model's path -> the share of its triangles kept at most (its coarsest level when none is that light) (Godot picks a batch's level by its nearest corner, so near batches drew every triangle). Remove a word to draw that plant whole. A wildflower's coarsest level is 785 of its 999 (its petals' open edges stay put), so its copies are fewer instead: countryside.json tuft_odds.
bulk._lod_px: bulk.gd: the most, in pixels on screen, a repeated small thing's simpler version (Godot's generated detail levels) may stray from it; each batch is judged at its copies' drawn size. Higher: lighter, coarser far off; 1 is near Godot's finest pick.

wild._bush_reach: vegetation.gd: bushes drawn out to this from the camera (was reach x 1.5, 36: the middle zoom's open country lost them, WC3's doodads stand at every zoom).
